links.outcome: Strict F1 of de-identification methods for detecting sensitive health information across datasets and settings
links.effect: Fine-tuned LLM trained on the combined corpus reached strict F1 0.9447; baseline best 0.8172; performance varied across heterogeneous EHR sources.
links.quote: Our findings indicate that while fine-tuned LLMs offer superior accuracy, the observed performance variability across heterogeneous electronic health record sources poses significant technical challenges.

links.outcome: Cross-dataset generalization of de-identification performance across training/testing combinations
links.effect: Nine training/testing settings assessed; the model trained on the combined corpus of all five datasets performed best, while performance varied across heterogeneous EHR sources.
links.quote: The experimental setup encompassed nine different settings using various combinations of training and testing sets to assess model robustness and cross-dataset performance.

unlisted_practices: Harmonising corpora and sensitive health information categories across datasets for de-identification
Supervised fine-tuning of LLMs on combined multi-source corpora to improve de-identification

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating LLM-based, rule-based, and hybrid models for clinical text de-identification across five datasets without evaluating a specific organizational deployment practice or operational safeguard.
